items.en:
Your quick-thinking bridge crew has provided a fake manifest on your behalf, of course.

Of course they would have a plausible but misleading pre-generated crew and passenger manifest ready for just such a situation. If you offered it with enough confidence - and very little delay - it might just work.

You wait with saintly patience as the Diktat officer has an underling run the fake manifest through the latest Diktat search and verification algorithms.

The old man goes calmly to the shuttle for transfer.

"Your service to the Supreme Executor will be noted in the official records," the Diktat $personRank says as if $heOrShe is reading a script for $hisOrHer bridge crew. "Your loyalty to the Great Movement is commended, and the reward for turning in a known terrorist will now be transferred to your accounts."

$PersonRank $personLastName performs a bizarre salute and shouts something about "final victory"; your comms officer manages to extract you from the comms-link without further exchange.

You have the old man and the kid transferred to the Sindrian Diktat flagship. They even want the robot "for evidence", so you have that old piece of junk sent as well.

"Your service to the Supreme Executor will be noted in the official records," $personRank $personLastName says like $heOrShe is reading a script for $hisOrHer bridge crew. "Your loyalty to the Great Movement is commended, and your reward for turning in a known terrorist and his accomplice will now be transferred."

$HeOrShe performs a bizarre salute and shouts something about "final victory"; your comms officer manages to extract you from the comm-link without further engagement.

"We shall take no prisoners!" the Diktat officer shouts, "Those who harbor terrorists are themselves terrorists, and will be treated as-"

The link cuts out. Your comms officer gives you an apologetic look.

You hear an angry call of "Run it again!" that perhaps was not intended to get picked up by comms. It takes a few more minutes. 

"Very well," the Diktat officer says with what sounds like clenched teeth, "Your manifest has been verified. Technically."

With a sharp motion, $heOrShe signals to $hisOrHer comms to cut the link.

And that's the end of it. You start to wonder how things might have gone differently if you'd carried out the job and snuck what was clearly some kind of former military officer and his protege into contact with a faction of the Askonian underground... 

You call to navigation to lay in a new course.

You receive a comms transmission from an obviously illicit orbital repeater which provides directions to a dropoff point for the old man, the kid, and their robot. And the promise of anonymous payment.

As they walk down the shuttle's ramp, the kid exclaims, "Wow, a planet made entirely of water!"
The kid manages not to look disappointed at this revelation.

You receive a comms transmission from an obviously illicit orbital repeater which provides directions to a dropoff point for the kid, and their robot. And the promise of payment.

The kid walks sullenly down the shuttle's ramp, his loyal robot trundling behind. As he steps onto the rolling deckplates of Volturn, he looks back.

"Take care of yourself, I guess," he says. "That's what you're best at, isn't it."
He looks like he's going to take the bait, but the robot bleeps at him, defusing his anger.

The kids gives you a look, a mix of sadness and a checked rage that you can tell will risk boiling over for a long time to come.

He turns to his robot. "Com'on, let's go," he says.
You're unable to safely deliver your passengers to Volturn right now.
The old man smiles and simply says, "Thank you, my friend," then turns up the hood of his robe and leads the strange party into the underworld of Volturn.

"Oh, you're one of those? Easy! Just go kill some Sindies," with a laugh, $heOrShe mimes shooting a pistol.

"Any questions?"

After a short wait and a burst of static the makeshift comms network of Umbra finally relays you through.

"Death to Andrada," she says as a greeting. "What do you want?"

"Back again." She gives you a look. "Did you forget something?"
OR
"Didn't you just comms?" She looks annoyed. "Out with it."

After a short wait and a burst of static the makeshift comms network of Umbra finally relays you through.

"Death to Andrada," she says as a greeting. "Captain $playerName, it's good to see you."

"Back again." She gives you a look. "Can I help you with something?"
OR
"Didn't you just comms?" She raises an eyebrow.

"Well, out with it."
"$playerName the liar." She scowls. "Didn't I tell you to suck vacuum?"

"The liar returns." She sniffs, and somehow looks down at you through the comms.

"Back to waste my time."

After a short wait and a burst of static the makeshift comms network of Umbra finally relays you through.

"Death to Andrada," she says as a greeting. Her eyes narrow as she takes you in.

"Aren't you... you're $playerName!"

She doesn't sound pleased to see you.
"No," she says deadpan. "Not good."
"No," she says deadpan. "I have not."

"You're a bloody-booted minion of the Diktat and I'll have you spaced for your crimes the moment I get the chance."

Her dimissal is backed by the arrogance of a gens-heir.

And is made complete as she slams the comms shut-off.
"What about him?" She watches you carefully.

She frowns, considering your claim.

"Could be. We don't think there's been a legitimate holo-cast from him for at least a cycle."

She shifts the tilt of her head. "But this raises two questions. One, why should we believe anything that comes from that ghoul Macario's mouth? Two, and this is the more pressing question to me, why in the name of Old Earth are you having personal conversations with Dolos Macario, Andrada's chief torturer and spymaster?"

You barely get half the words out before Imoinu speaks forcefully over you.

"I don't care about Macario's lies! Answer my question. How are you talking to him?"

"A merc." Imoinu crosses her arms. "So you only believe in credits. Good for you."

"Did Macario hire you to spread his lies for him? Don't bother answering."

"And I suppose you're acting as a double agent to take them down from the inside, somehow."

She considers you, though from her face it is clear that her opinion of your methods and their chance of success is not high.

"Okay." She crosses her arms. "I don't think that changes anything."

"And I suppose you're acting as a double agent to take them down from the inside, somehow."

She considers you, though from her face it is clear that her opinion of your methods and their chance of success is not high.

"Okay." She crosses her arms. "I appreciate... the ARC and the United Front appreciate your contribution to the cause."
"Sure. Okay." She crosses her arms and gives you an incredulous look.
"No you're not." Imoinu crosses her arms. "You're as much a liar as Macario."

"No you're not." Imoinu crosses her arms. "You already used that line on us and it was a lie the first time."

"Did Macario hire you to spread his lies for him? Don't bother answering."

"A Luddic, huh." She has an odd expression, a crease in her brow. Like there's some deep-seated disgust that she's trying to hide.

"Well. Blessings to you, I guess," she says awkwardly. "I don't know whether to believe you or not. You should probably connect with Standfast and the VSDC. Anyway..."

"Finlay Siyavong? Ha!"

You can hear the aristocrat in her laugh. It is bitter, and a potential for sharp cruelty hides there.

"I've met him, you fool. You're not Finlay Siyavong. You're a liar."

"If what you say is true about Andrada, then it's probably good news. Probably. But practically speaking it doesn't change the situation. Holos can be faked. It's the entire basis of the Diktat propaganda machine."

She shrugs. "Besides, the Sindrian Diktat lives on, run by Andrada's underlings. The worlds of Askonia are still held under the boot of the oppressor. The fight must go on."

"And even if you weren't lying about Andrada, practically speaking it doesn't change the situation. Holos can be faked. It's the entire basis of the Diktat propaganda machine."

She shrugs. "The Sindrian Diktat lives on, run by Andrada's underlings in his name. The worlds of Askonia are still held under the boot of the oppressor. The fight must go on."

"Yeah, what of it?"

She sticks her chin up, striking what is intended to be a defiant expression.

"I'm here to fight the brutal oppressions and liberate the Askonian System!"

She looks at you suspiciously for a long moment.

"For a 'supporter', your words reek of defeatism. We need material support, not misplaced admonition."

"A pathetic attempt to ingratiate yourself after your previous blunder. Your ruse wouldn't work on a child." Her eyes narrow.

"Tell me, are you another freelancer hired by my grandmother to come admonish me? Tell her she's wasted her credits."
"We have nothing to talk about," she snaps, then hits the comms cut-off.
"That's right," she says. "Now did you have anything useful to say, or are we done?"

"He is." She looks taken aback, but quickly recovers her composure.

"You met him? He's still on Mazalot suppressing the Luddics for the gens, I suppose."

"You don't say!"

She laughs. You can hear the echo of long-running sibling conflict.

"Of course he's angry. He's there on behalf of the gens to hammer the Luddic faithful into compliant citizens of the League! The only tools he can imagine are force and fear because he thinks the Luddics are irrational sub-humans. Like stupid, simple animals."

She shakes her head, "He can't help but fail."

"Dardan, helpful?" She scoffs. "Doesn't sound like him."

"He's there on behalf of the gens to hammer the Luddic faithful into compliant citizens of the League! The only tools he can imagine are force and fear because he thinks the Luddics are irrational sub-humans. Like stupid, simple animals."

She shakes her head, "He can't help but fail."

"You don't say!"

She laughs. You can hear the echo of long-running sibling conflict.

"Of course he's unhappy. He's there on behalf of the gens to hammer the Luddic faithful into compliant citizens of the League! The only tools he can imagine are force and fear because he thinks the Luddics are irrational sub-humans. Like stupid, simple animals."

She shakes her head, "He can't help but fail."

"Of course they object," she says. "They're part of an aristocratic elite whose position is predicated on the extractive exploitation of the masses."

 A hint of a smile appears. "And I've chosen to fight everything they stand for."
